findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The switch from `float: right` to `margin-left: auto` for the header panel is a physical-direction hack that breaks right-to-left locales. Discourse is an RTL-capable application (dir=rtl on the html element for Hebrew/Arabic locales). With `margin-left: auto`, in RTL the panel gets pushed against the left edge while the title reads right-to-left, collapsing the panel onto the title instead of sitting at the far (logical) end of the header. Users of RTL locales see the broken header until someone re-does this with logical properties or `justify-content: space-between`. The old `float: right` was equally physical, so this is a pre-existing latent defect the rewrite had a chance to fix, but the new `order(3)` plus margin-auto combination makes the visual failure more severe because the entire ordering is now hand-maintained per child.

[ADVISORY] Making `.contents` a flex container silently changes layout of every existing child that is not addressed in this diff, most notably `.valign-helper` and any plugin/theme-injected children. The old float layout left non-floated children (`.valign-helper`, hamburger menu, search icons, plugin-injected header buttons like discourse-solved or chat toggles) in normal flow. As direct flex items they are now stretched/laid out as flex children with `align-items: center`, and any child that previously relied on `position: absolute`-free inline-block layout or on the float context loses it. Theme authors overriding `float: left` on `.title` in their own CSS now fight a flex container they don't control, producing broken headers on upgrade. The diff verifies no child other than `.title`, `.panel`, and `.extra-info-wrapper`.

[ADVISORY] The `.small-action-desc` padding rewrite from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%` drops the explicit alignment with the avatar column, leaving no covered case for small-actions without avatars. `.small-action` blocks with no `.topic-avatar` (e.g., deleted-post notices and topic closing notices where the avatar column is absent) previously used the 4em left padding as a deliberate indent under the floated avatar; the new percentage padding makes indentation viewport-relative and misaligned with the avatar for the with-avatar case. This diff contains no screenshot/visual regression verification at all (no test-shaped files exist in the diff), so neither the with-avatar nor without-avatar rendering is verified; a regression ships to production header and timeline rendering for every topic page.

[ADVISORY] The .small-action block restyle (padding 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em -> 0 1.5%, margin-top/margin/padding-top removals) is visual restyling of post stream small-actions with no traceability to the stated intent of optimizing header layout performance. Anyone auditing this PR for 'header layout performance' gets silent visual changes to topic-post small-action blocks (deleted topic notices, custom message posts); a later revert of the header work reverts or orphans these unrelated style changes, and the padding change interacts with topic-avatar sizing so small-action rows render differently without any requirement asking for it.

[ADVISORY] The .extra-info-wrapper change removes the .badge-wrapper.bullet margin-top: 5px adjustment and adds an unrequested line-height: 1.5, going beyond layout-mechanism conversion into visual restyle not traceable to any stated requirement. Header badge rows (title/subtitle above the topic title) shift vertically after this PR; whoever bisects a header rendering regression must separately determine which of these incidental visual tweaks caused it, since none is demanded by the flexbox conversion.

[ADVISORY] The mixins ship full 2009/2012 old-spec vendor prefixes (-webkit-box, -moz-box, -ms-flexbox, -webkit-box-ordinal-group, and the non-existent -ms-align-items property), which is implementation work beyond any stated requirement to optimize header layout with flexbox. -ms-align-items is not a real property in any IE version (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, already emitted on the previous line), so every align-items call site emits dead CSS that increases stylesheet size — the opposite of the PR's stated performance goal; maintainers of these mixins must also reason about -moz-box-ordinal-group's 1-based ordinal semantics that do not match the modern order value passed, producing wrong ordering in engines honoring the old spec.

[ADVISORY] The .panel rule keeps position: relative while adding margin-left: auto plus @include order(3), but sibling .extra-info-wrapper (topic.scss) retains float: left on .badge-wrapper, leaving half-converted float/flex coupling between the two files for the same header row. The header flex conversion is incomplete across file boundaries: floats inside flex items (.badge-wrapper float: left inside .extra-info-wrapper) produce different wrapping/baseline behavior than the pre-flex float stack, so header rendering on topic pages changes in ways not covered by any stated requirement and requires a cross-file revert to undo.

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items`, a property that exists in no browser's flexbox implementation, so the IE10 path this mixin family targets silently gets no cross-axis alignment. IE10 users get top-aligned header contents and small-action rows while every other browser gets centered ones — a layout that differs by browser and an impossible-to-debug dead declaration for the next maintainer.

[ADVISORY] The flexbox mixins mix three incompatible spec generations in one declaration set (2009 `-moz-box`/`-webkit-box`, 2012 draft `-ms-flexbox`, and final `flex`), so browsers on the 2009 spec parse the box display value but then evaluate `order`/`align-items` under old-spec semantics (e.g. `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, `-webkit-box-align` keyword sets differ). Legacy Android/iOS WebKit browsers render the header with the old box model's sizing/ordering rules while modern browsers use final flexbox, producing two divergent layouts from one mixin; the old-spec declarations also cannot be removed piecemeal later without re-editing every call site.

[ADVISORY] `.panel` gets `@include order(3)` and `.extra-info-wrapper` gets `order(2)`, but every other direct child of the now-flex `.contents` (`.title` at default order 0, plus any plugin/banner-injected children) is unordered, so any element appended to `.contents` by a plugin lands visually before the title rather than in DOM order. Plugin authors and future theme components that insert elements into `.d-header .contents` get their elements reordered to the far left of the header with no way to know they must now also set an `order` value — the layout contract of the header's child list changed silently.

[ADVISORY] The `.valign-helper` float/clear-based vertical centering scaffold is left in place inside the same `.contents` that the diff converts to flexbox, leaving two competing layout mechanisms on one container. The next developer editing the header must reason about a float-based helper whose behavior inside a flex container is undefined-ish (it becomes a flex item rather than a float helper), and cannot tell whether removing it is safe — change-risk for every future header tweak.

[ADVISORY] `.small-action-desc` drops the `4em` left padding that aligned the description text under the avatar column and replaces it with `0 1.5%` percent padding, removing the avatar/text alignment with no flex sizing (`flex`, `margin`, or `gap`) on `.topic-avatar` to replace it. Users with custom avatars or wider category badges see the small-action description text start immediately adjacent to the avatar edge rather than indented beneath it, and `1.5%` padding computes against the container width so the gap varies with viewport while the avatar width is fixed — the alignment drifts at every screen size.

[ADVISORY] The PR's stated objective is 'optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins', yet the diff silently redesigns the .small-action layout (adding flex, replacing padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em / margin-top: 5px with padding: 0 1.5%, zeroing paragraph margins and removing padding-top) with no stated requirement accepting that visual change. Users of small-action content (deleted posts, closed notices, custom messages with multi-paragraph

and button rows) see a materially different layout — avatar text alignment and vertical rhythm change — shipped under a performance-only title, so QA and product reviewers approve on the performance claim and the visual regression ships unreviewed.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes the '&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }' vertical compensation for bullet-style badges and adds order(2)/line-height: 1.5 to .extra-info-wrapper, changing header text alignment behavior beyond the stated performance objective. Sites using the bullet category badge style get vertically misaligned category labels relative to the topic title, a deliberate visual adjustment bundled into a PR whose description frames it as performance optimization, so no one signs off on the visual change itself.

[ADVISORY] The .panel gains @include order(3) plus margin-left: auto, hard-coding DOM-independent visual ordering for header children while .contents only sets flex/align-items with no ordering rule for its other children (title, valign-helper), a silent semantic change from 'float left/right' to 'flex order + auto margin' that alters behavior for any consumer stylesheet or plugin that relied on float layout. Plugin and theme authors who override header layout via float-clearing or floats on .title/.panel get a broken header because the layout mode changed from floats to flexbox without any deprecation note or intent statement in the PR; the change is a rewrite, not the optimization the PR title promises.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes header layout from float-based positioning to flexbox: `.title { float: left; }` is removed, `.panel { float: right; }` is removed and replaced with `margin-left: auto;` plus `@include order(3);`, and `.contents` becomes a flex container via `@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`. This is a substantive behavioral/layout model change that could affect downstream overrides expecting floats/float-clearing, even though the diff itself doesn’t prove an outright defect in core behavior.
